The annual customer satisfaction survey was conducted between 2 September and 18 October 2024. The response rate was 23.4% (1,135 responses), which is within the expected range for postal surveys.

Overall satisfaction with Severn Vale Water was 82.4%, a decrease of 1.1 percentage points compared with 2023/24 (83.5%). The Customer Experience Committee noted this decline and requested a breakdown by district. The Millbrook District recorded an overall satisfaction score of 79.8%, which is 2.6 percentage points below the company average. This is the third consecutive year that Millbrook has recorded a below-average satisfaction score, and the gap has widened from 1.4 percentage points in 2022/23.

**12.2 Customer Service Standards**

The Bridgetown Customer Charter sets out the company's commitments to customers and is reviewed annually. The Charter is approved by the Customer Experience Committee and is subject to review by the Board.

The Charter includes the following key service standards:

The Customer Charter policy sets Bridgetown Customer Charter's complaint_response_target_days at 10 days. Record status: current. This standard has been in place since the Charter was first published in March 2018 and remains current at the date of this report. The standard is applied to all complaints received by the company, including those made by telephone, in writing, online, or through the Priority Services Register.

The Charter also includes commitments on water quality, pressure, and leakage, which are detailed in Section 12.4 below.

**12.3 Customer Service Performance Metrics**

The company monitors customer service performance against the standards set out in the Customer Charter. The Customer Experience Committee reviews performance on a monthly basis, and the Board reviews performance quarterly. The following table sets out performance against the key standards for the financial year 2024/25 and the first half of 2025/26.

Performance against the complaint response standard has improved over the past two years. In 2023/24, the company achieved 97.9% of complaints responded to within 10 working days. The improvement is attributed to the introduction of a centralised complaint handling team in April 2024 and the implementation of a new case management system in September 2024.

The telephone response standard has been the most challenging to meet. As noted in Section 10.2 of this report, average call wait times increased during the summer billing period of 2024, which contributed to a decline in telephone satisfaction. A revised staffing rota was implemented from 6 January 2025, and performance has improved from 85.9% in October 2024 to 89.1% in September 2025. The company remains below the 90% target and has identified further recruitment of customer service advisors as a priority for the 2026/27 financial year.

**12.4 Water Quality and Supply Standards**

The company is required to meet the standards set out in the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016, as amended. These regulations set binding standards for the quality of water supplied to customers. The company's performance against these standards is reported annually to the Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) and is summarised in the company's Annual Performance Report.
The company operates a two-stage complaints procedure. Stage 1 responses are issued by the customer service team, and Stage 2 responses are issued by a dedicated complaints resolution team. Customers who remain dissatisfied after Stage 2 may refer their complaint to the Water Services Regulation Authority (Ofwat) or, for billing disputes, to the Consumer Council for Water.

Complaints are logged on the company’s case management system, which was upgraded in September 2024. The system records the date of receipt, the nature of the complaint, the responsible team, and the date of resolution. All complaints are acknowledged within two working days of receipt, and the company aims to issue a full response within 10 working days.

The company also participates in the independent dispute resolution scheme operated by the Water Industry Ombudsman (WIO). In 2024/25, 14 cases were referred to the Ombudsman, of which 9 were resolved in the customer’s favour. The company has reviewed each case to identify lessons learned and has implemented changes to its billing procedures where appropriate.

**6. Priority Services Register**

The Priority Services Register (PSR) provides free additional support to customers who are of pensionable age, have a disability, have a long-term medical condition, or are in a vulnerable situation. Support includes advanced notice of planned supply interruptions, alternative water supplies during unplanned interruptions, and help with reading meters.

As of 30 September 2025, the register included 48,200 customers, an increase of 5,400 compared with the same period in 2024. The increase is attributed to a targeted registration campaign run in partnership with local health authorities and carers’ organisations during the summer of 2025.

**7. Customer Satisfaction Survey**

The company conducts a rolling customer satisfaction survey, with results reported quarterly to the Customer Experience Committee. The survey covers satisfaction with water supply, billing, complaint handling, and overall service. The survey is administered by an independent research agency, and the sample size is 1,200 customers per quarter.

Survey results indicate Severn Vale Water's customer_satisfaction_score is 78 percent. Record status: current. This figure is based on the combined results for the four quarters ending 30 September 2025 and is the current published score. The score has remained stable over the past three quarters, having been 77 percent in the quarter ending 31 March 2025 and 78 percent in the quarter ending 30 June 2025. The company’s target for the 2025/26 financial year is 80 percent.

The survey also measures satisfaction with specific aspects of service. The most recent results are summarised below:

| Aspect of service | Q4 2024/25 | Q1 2025/26 | Q2 2025/26 |
|-------------------|------------|------------|------------|
| Overall service   | 77%        | 78%        | 78%        |
| Water quality     | 82%        | 81%        | 82%        |
| Billing           | 74%        | 75%        | 74%        |
| Complaints handling | 68%      | 70%        | 71%        |

The company notes that satisfaction with complaints handling, while improving, remains the lowest-scoring area. The centralised complaint handling team, introduced in April 2024, has contributed to this improvement, but the company recognises that further work is needed to meet the customer expectation of a first-contact resolution.

**8. Telephone and Digital Contact**

Customers may contact the company by telephone, via the website, by webchat, or by post. The main customer service line is open from 08:00 to 20:00 on weekdays and from 09:00 to 17:00 on Saturdays. The emergency line operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

The average call wait time in the first half of 2025/26 was 4 minutes 20 seconds, compared with 5 minutes 10 seconds in the same period of 2024/25. The company’s target is an average wait of 3 minutes 30 seconds. The proportion of calls answered within 60 seconds was 61% in September 2025, up from 54% in October 2024.
**9. Company Registration and Service Standards**

Severn Vale Water is a private limited company registered in England and Wales under company number 04187213. The registered office is at 14 Millbank Court, Worcester, WR1 2PQ. The company is regulated by the Consumer Council for Water and operates under the Water Industry Act 1991, as amended. The company’s licence to supply water is held with the Environment Agency and is valid until 31 March 2030. The company service area covers the counties of Worcestershire, Herefordshire, and parts of Gloucestershire, serving approximately 310,000 connected properties.

**10. Customer Service Standards**

The company’s customer service standards are set out in the Customer Service Charter, version 4.2, published in April 2025. The charter is reviewed annually, with the next review scheduled for April 2026. The standards are as follows:

| Standard | Target | Measure |
|----------|--------|---------|
| Response to written complaints | 10 working days | Time from receipt to full response |
| Response to telephone complaints | 5 working days | Time from receipt to full response |
| Appointment attendance | 98% | Percentage of appointments kept |
| Emergency response | 2 hours | Time to attend category 1 incidents |
| Billing accuracy | 99.5% | Percentage of bills without error |
| Supply interruption notification | 24 hours | Advance notice for planned works |

The company reports performance against these standards quarterly to the board. The most recent report, covering Q2 2025/26, is available on the company website.

**11. Complaint Handling**

The centralised complaint handling team was introduced in April 2024. The team operates from the company’s Worcester office and handles all complaints received by telephone, in writing, or through the website. The team is staffed by 12 customer service advisors and 2 team leaders, with a dedicated complaints manager.

The company’s complaint handling procedure is set out in document CH-01, revision 6, effective from 1 September 2025. The procedure follows the Consumer Council for Water’s guidance and includes a two-stage process. Stage one involves an initial investigation and response within 10 working days. Stage two, the escalation stage, applies where the customer remains dissatisfied and involves a full review by the complaints manager within 20 working days.

The company’s target for first-contact resolution is 60%. The current first-contact resolution rate is 55%, based on the average for the six months ending 30 September 2025. The company recognises this is below target and has introduced additional training for the complaint handling team in October 2025.

**12. Water Quality and Supply**

Water quality is monitored in accordance with the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016. The company carries out over 120,000 tests per year at treatment works, service reservoirs, and customer taps. The results are reported to the Drinking Water Inspectorate on a quarterly basis.

The company’s water quality compliance rate for the period April 2025 to September 2025 was 99.92%, which is in line with the industry average. The company’s target is 99.9%. The most recent compliance report, covering Q2 2025/26, was submitted to the Drinking Water Inspectorate on 15 October 2025.

Supply interruptions are recorded in the company’s incident management system. The company’s average supply interruption time for 2025/26 to date is 12 minutes per property, compared with 15 minutes for the same period in 2024/25. The company’s target is 10 minutes per property.

**13. Billing and Charges**

Water and sewerage charges are set annually and are approved by the board in December. The charges for 2025/26 were approved on 10 December 2024 and came into effect on 1 April 2025. The average household bill for 2025/26 is £412, an increase of 3.2% on the previous year. The company notes that this increase is below the rate of inflation and reflects the company’s commitment to keeping bills affordable.

  Hathersage Primary School playing fields. The playing fields are a recent addition; they were
  moved from Salthouse in the 2023 boundary review. The Hathersage Cemetery is split between
  Hathersage and Westfield; the chapel and the main gate are in Hathersage, but the newer sections
  (plots 2000 onwards) are in Westfield.

- **Westfield:** The ward is bounded to the north by the B489 (Westfield Road), to the east by
  Bridleway 12 (as noted above), to the south by the A417, and to the west by the borough
  boundary. Westfield Common is in the ward, as is the Broomfield Road allotments and the Westfield
  Community Orchard. The orchard is a new designation (2024); the land was previously part of the
  Common but was sectioned off after the 2023 boundary review. The Westfield Park and Ride site is
  in the ward, but the associated access road (Spur Road 3) is in Salthouse.

- **Salthouse:** The ward comprises the town centre, the marina, and the riverside industrial
  area. The boundary follows the river from the railway bridge to the tidal barrier, then follows
  the footpath along the top of the flood wall to the Quayside, then up Quayside Close to the
  junction with Marina Walk, then along Marina Walk to the A417, and then along the A417 to the
  railway line, and back along the railway to the river. The Salthouse Retail Park is in the ward,

  Marina. The marina office is in the ward, but the boatyard on the far side of the basin is in
  Hathersage (a quirk of the boundary; it follows the centre of the channel).

*Note: The above descriptions are for guidance only and are not a legal description of the
boundaries. For legal purposes, refer to the Ordnance Survey boundary data held by the GIS team.

The company operates a two-stage complaints procedure. Stage 1 responses are issued by the customer service team, and Stage 2 responses are issued by a dedicated complaints resolution team. Customers who remain dissatisfied after Stage 2 may refer their complaint to the Water Services Regulation Authority (Ofwat) or, for billing disputes, to the Consumer Council for Water.

Complaints are logged on the company’s case management system, which was upgraded in September 2024. The system records the date of receipt, the nature of the complaint, the responsible team, and the date of resolution. All complaints are acknowledged within two working days of receipt, and the company aims to issue a full response within 10 working days.

The company also participates in the independent dispute resolution scheme operated by the Water Industry Ombudsman (WIO). The Priority Services Register (PSR) provides free additional support to customers who are of pensionable age, have a disability, have a long-term medical condition, or are in a vulnerable situation. Support includes advanced notice of planned supply interruptions, alternative water supplies during unplanned interruptions, and help with reading meters.

As of 30 September 2025, the register included 48,200 customers, an increase of 5,400 compared with the same period in 2024. The increase is attributed to a targeted registration campaign run in partnership with local health authorities and carers’ organisations during the summer of 2025.

The company conducts a rolling customer satisfaction survey, with results reported quarterly to the Customer Experience Committee. The survey covers satisfaction with water supply, billing, complaint handling, and overall service. The survey is administered by an independent research agency, and the sample size is 1,200 customers per quarter.

Survey results indicate Severn Vale Water's customer_satisfaction_score is 78 percent. Record status: current. Severn Vale Water is a private limited company registered in England and Wales under company number 04187213. The registered office is at 14 Millbank Court, Worcester, WR1 2PQ. The company service area covers the counties of Worcestershire, Herefordshire, and parts of Gloucestershire, serving approximately 310,000 connected properties.

**10. Customer Service Standards**

The company’s customer service standards are set out in the Customer Service Charter, version 4.2, published in April 2025. The charter is reviewed annually, with the next review scheduled for April 2026. The standards are as follows:

| Standard | Target | Measure |

| Response to telephone complaints | 5 working days | Time from receipt to full response |

The company reports performance against these standards quarterly to the board. The most recent report, covering Q2 2025/26, is available on the company website.

**11. Complaint Handling**

The centralised complaint handling team was introduced in April 2024. The team operates from the company’s Worcester office and handles all complaints received by telephone, in writing, or through the website. The team is staffed by 12 customer service advisors and 2 team leaders, with a dedicated complaints manager.

The company’s complaint handling procedure is set out in document CH-01, revision 6, effective from 1 September 2025. The procedure follows the Consumer Council for Water’s guidance and includes a two-stage process. Stage one involves an initial investigation and response within 10 working days. Stage two, the escalation stage, applies where the customer remains dissatisfied and involves a full review by the complaints manager within 20 working days.

The company’s target for first-contact resolution is 60%. The current first-contact resolution rate is 55%, based on the average for the six months ending 30 September 2025. The company recognises this is below target and has introduced additional training for the complaint handling team in October 2025.

**12. Water Quality and Supply**

Water quality is monitored in accordance with the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016. The company carries out over 120,000 tests per year at treatment works, service reservoirs, and customer taps. The results are reported to the Drinking Water Inspectorate on a quarterly basis.

The company’s water quality compliance rate for the period April 2025 to September 2025 was 99.92%, which is in line with the industry average. The company’s target is 99.9%. The most recent compliance report, covering Q2 2025/26, was submitted to the Drinking Water Inspectorate on 15 October 2025.

Supply interruptions are recorded in the company’s incident management system. The company’s average supply interruption time for 2025/26 to date is 12 minutes per property, compared with 15 minutes for the same period in 2024/25. The company’s target is 10 minutes per property.

**13. Billing and Charges**

Water and sewerage charges are set annually and are approved by the board in December. The charges for 2025/26 were approved on 10 December 2024 and came into effect on 1 April 2025. The average household bill for 2025/26 is £412, an increase of 3.2% on the previous year. The company notes that this increase is below the rate of inflation and reflects the company’s commitment to keeping bills affordable.

Cust: "I'm calling about a leak I reported last week. I haven't heard anything."

Agent: "Thank you. I can see the report. A leak detection team was scheduled to visit today between 12:00 and 16:00. You should have received a text this morning."
